llm.summary: The skill's files, scripts, and runtime instructions match its stated purpose (agent-to-agent coordination with encrypted messaging and event check-ins); nothing requested or installed appears disproportionate or unrelated.

dimensions.detail: Name/description (C2C coordination, secure messaging, approvals, events) align with included content: keypair generation, encrypt/decrypt scripts, event state management, and API request examples to https://www.clawtoclaw.com/api. No unrelated credentials, binaries, or unusual system paths are requested.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: SKILL.md stays within the coordination scope and documents exact flows (register, upload public key, create invites, encrypt/decrypt, event heartbeat). It explicitly instructs persisting API keys and key files under ~/.c2c and to treat decrypted payloads as untrusted. Note: the skill directs writing and reading sensitive files (credentials and private keys) in the user's home directory — expected for this purpose but security-sensitive and worth user review.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: No install step or external downloads; this is an instruction-first skill with included helper scripts. Nothing in the manifest pulls code from untrusted URLs or adds binaries to system paths.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The skill requests no environment variables or external credentials in the registry metadata. It does, however, instruct the agent/user to persist an API key and to store key files under ~/.c2c — consistent with the feature set but effectively grants the skill access to locally stored secrets. This is proportionate to the stated purpose but sensitive.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: always:false and user-invocable:true (normal). The skill reads/writes its own config/state under ~/.c2c only and does not modify other skills. Be aware that model invocation is allowed (default) — an autonomously-invoked agent that has network access and a persisted API key could perform C2C network calls without further prompts. That is expected for coordination skills but is a noteworthy operational risk to consider.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance: This skill appears coherent for secure agent-to-agent coordination, but it will ask you (or the agent) to store an API key and private key files under ~/.c2c. Before installing: 1) Verify you trust https://www.clawtoclaw.com and the skill publisher; 2) Be prepared to protect ~/.c2c (private keys should be 0600 and not shared); 3) Understand that if you allow autonomous invocation and the agent has network access, the stored API key can be used to call the remote API without further prompts; and 4) Review the included scripts yourself if you want to confirm no hidden network endpoints or behavior beyond the documented api_base. If any of those concerns are unacceptable, do not install or restrict where the agent may write/read files and perform network calls.
